reviews.title: Well Built w/ anti-slip material
reviews.comment:
Overall, I am impressed with this Asus ROG Hone Ace. Which, I bought this to replace my old Razer Strider mouse mat. I use this space for work, studying (college), and gaming.
+ Positives
1. I have had this mat for a couple of weeks, it appears to be well-built.
+ The stitching is tightly wound, it appears fraying will not occur anytime soon.
2. The surface is smooth, that said, my keyboard (ASUS ROG Claymore II) does not move unless I physically relocate it. However, my mouse (ASUS ROG Harpe Ace) glides effortlessly across the mat.
3. The memory foam is firm and yet there is just enough give to be comfortable.
4. Anti-slip material on the bottom guarantees the mat stays in place and does not bunch up.
Note: the anti-slip material almost feels like a sticker, so far, no residue has been left behind on my real wood desk.
5.  Easy to clean
+ Does not catch or hold as much debris as my old Razer mouse mat.
Example: I have a Siberian Husky and his hair blows right off the mat.
6. Low profile design
- Negative(s)
1. (Nitpick) As can be seen at the bottom of the picture. The mouse mat is not straight across, the middle has a slight inward curve.
Note: Not sure if this was intentional.
Given the initial impression of quality, even under heavy use, there is potential for this mat to last for several years. Hopefully, the reliability justifies the higher price over other mats.
Recommendation: Need a quality sturdy and comfortable mouse mat. Plus, do not like replacing items every couple of years. I would recommend this mat.
reviews.author: RA

reviews.title: Overall Great Mousepad.
reviews.comment: I’m impressed with the Asus ROG Hone Ace, which I purchased to replace my old Razer Strider mouse mat. I use this space for work, studying (college), and gaming, and so far, this mat has exceeded expectations. After a couple of weeks, it’s clear that it’s well-built, with tightly wound stitching that seems resistant to fraying. The surface is smooth and performs excellently. The memory foam base is firm but has just enough give to be comfortable, and the anti-slip material underneath ensures the mat doesn’t shift or bunch up, even during intense use. Interestingly, the anti-slip layer almost feels like a sticker, but it hasn’t left any residue on my real wood desk. Another standout feature is how easy it is to clean; it doesn’t trap debris like my old mat, and even my Siberian Husky’s fur doesn’t stick—it blows right off. I also appreciate the low-profile design, which keeps the workspace looking clean and minimal. My only minor complaint is a slight inward curve along the bottom edge of the mat, which may or may not be intentional, but it’s purely aesthetic. Overall, the quality of this mat suggests it could last for several years, and if durability matches the build, the higher price is justified. If you’re looking for a high-quality, sturdy, and comfortable mouse mat and prefer not to replace your gear every couple of years, I would recommend the ROG Hone Ace.
reviews.author: Logan

reviews.title: Great mat, no creases
reviews.comment: Looks like they resolved the wrinkle/creases issue by shipping with a large stiff cardboard cylinder. Just got mine it sits perfectly flat. Has a nice texture. Little bit of stick to the underside to keep it in place. If this mouse pad can stay stain free from my mouse hand for more than 6 mo. I'll keep it 5 stars.
reviews.author: Steve

reviews.title: Really good mouse pad.
reviews.comment: It was a lot bigger than I thought it would be but it's still very nice and my mouse glides and tracks well on it. It feels very nice and its thickness and durability are great.
reviews.author: Jackson Miller

reviews.title: High Quality, Feels great
reviews.comment:
The second I took this mat out of the box I could immediately tell it was of a much higher quality than my previous $20 XL mousepad. Glide is amazing, immensely better than my last one. Price is steep on this one for a reason, but I know I wont be needing to replace it for years to come. Would recommend.
*noticed some people having issues with it not laying flat but I didn't have any issues there. The bottom of the pad has some sort of adhesive on it so it sticks pretty firmly to the desk. Don't expect to move it around a bunch without losing some of that adhesiveness. I'd even go as far as recommending laying out some sort of indicator like tape or something so you can line it up perfectly when you lay it out the first time.
